name: code_read_file
description: Read one file of Ledgerline's private codebase by its exact path, as code_search prints it: relative to the repository root and case-sensitive, so src/Report.ts and src/report.tsx are different files. config/ is never readable. Returns JSON {path, total_lines, start_line, end_line, truncated, next_start_line, content}. Every response is capped: concise returns at most 150 lines, detailed at most 600, and either at most 20,000 characters; when truncated is true, call again with start_line set to next_start_line to read on. An empty file is a success with content "" and total_lines 0: there is nothing in it. A path that does not exist is an error that names the nearest paths that do; retry with one of them exactly, never the same path again.

path.description: The file's path relative to the repository root, exactly as a code_search result printed it, case included: src/api/router.ts. No leading /, no .., no directories.

response_format.description: concise, the cheap default: at most 150 lines of the file as it is, enough for most source files here. detailed: at most 600 lines, each prefixed with its line number, about 10% more tokens per line; choose it to cite exact lines or to read a long file in one call.

start_line.description: null starts at line 1, the usual choice. A line number, from 1, starts there: the next_start_line of a truncated read, or a line a search hit named. Past the end of the file is an error that gives the file's length.

examples.note: Typical: a path exactly as a search result printed it, from the top, concise.
Hard: a .tsx file, not .ts; a search hit at line 28, so start a little before it, with line numbers to cite. A near-miss name (ReportTable.ts, reporttable.tsx) is an error naming this path.
